title: AI subscription value: count the work, then the tokens
summary: A source-checked guide to API-equivalent value, real subscription costs and cost per accepted result, with a client-only calculator.

editorial.headline: What is your AI subscription actually worth?
editorial.dek: The 5× chart asks a useful question. A transparent calculator helps answer it for your own workload.

sections.heading: The headline is about a meter. Your decision is about work.
paragraphs: A circulating chart says Anthropic subscriptions deliver more than five times OpenAI’s value. The claim is worth examining, but its unit matters: API-equivalent dollars estimate what an assumed token workload would cost at public API prices. They do not measure cash refunded, provider compute expense, hours saved or finished work. A generous allowance can be valuable; an allowance you cannot use is still unused capacity.

For a small studio, an IndustryNext project or a UES workflow, the useful question is narrower: which setup gets the required result accepted, on time, at the lowest total cost? PointCast’s calculator makes that question testable without asking for account access or private billing files.

sections.heading: What the original research establishes
paragraphs: SemiAnalysis published the original analysis on October 5, 2026. Its public methodology measures token categories against subscription-meter movements, discards incomplete steps and seeks rate ranges within ±5%. It then applies its own September agentic workload mix. It treats cache reads as free when 500 million reads produce no meter movement. That is a disclosed measurement assumption, not a promise from either provider.

The supplied chart reports $2,084 versus $11,726 of API-equivalent use on the $200 tiers. That is about 5.63×. PointCast has not replicated the experiment or accessed the paid dashboard and raw logs. The screenshot’s tiny workload percentages are not reliable enough to import as calculator defaults.

sections.heading: The price tag changes the apparent value
paragraphs: Official standard, short-context rates put GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 per million ordinary input tokens, $0.10 cached input and $10 output. Claude Opus 5.5 lists $4, $0.20 and $20, respectively. Corresponding short-lived cache writes are $2.50 and $5. Identical quantities in those four billing categories therefore receive twice the API valuation under the Opus rate card.

That arithmetic does not prove either model is twice as capable or that both consume identical tokens to solve a task. It shows why API-equivalent value combines quantity with a vendor’s list price. A price cut can shrink that headline metric while making an API customer’s actual bill smaller. Tokenization, reasoning settings and tool behavior make matched-task testing more informative than matched token counts.

sections.heading: A subscription is not a fixed monthly token bag
paragraphs: The current OpenAI page lists Plus at $20 and Pro at $100, $200 and $500 per month. It explicitly separates API pricing from included subscription usage. Work and Codex share usage; Pro currently has no five-hour cap, while weekly limits may apply. Anthropic lists Pro at $20 monthly and Max web subscriptions at $100 or $200, with five-hour and weekly limits.

Those windows matter. Someone who can work only on Friday cannot automatically collect every reset that occurred earlier in the week. Model-specific restrictions and shared usage across surfaces also affect what remains available. Check the account’s actual dashboard and renewal terms; a three-bar comparison cannot represent every current plan or account.

sections.heading: Caching rewards a particular kind of work
paragraphs: An agent repeatedly reading a stable repository or document can generate a huge cache-read count. That is different from repeatedly generating new long answers. A cache hit reuses eligible context; it is not a fresh output token. Writes, cache lifetimes and cache misses also have prices. A calculator that prices every input token as uncached will exaggerate API cost for a cache-heavy job.

Use mutually exclusive counts for ordinary input, cache reads, cache writes and output. Include billed reasoning where applicable, tool charges and paid execution resources. Select the correct context length and processing tier. The published presets are reference snapshots; a discounted batch rate, premium speed mode or negotiated rate requires a different calculation.

sections.heading: Measure accepted results
paragraphs: Pick a repeatable task and define acceptance before running it: a comparison whose sources check out, a design meeting its brief, or code that passes specified tests. Count every attempt, abandoned run and correction. Record accepted tasks, elapsed time, hands-on review minutes and spending. Keep the task scope and acceptance standard stable across candidates.

A hypothetical $100 setup with $20 in extras and five review hours at $75 per hour costs $495. A $20 setup needing eight review hours costs $620. If each produces 40 accepted results, their effective costs are $12.38 and $15.50 per result. These invented numbers demonstrate the method; they are not evidence of either provider’s quality.

sections.heading: A small test beats a universal winner
paragraphs: Choose three ordinary jobs and one demanding job that you genuinely need done. Give both candidates the same source material, deadline and acceptance checklist. Let each use its normal tools, but record any missing feature or manual workaround. Review outputs without looking at the bill first, then compare the complete costs.

Keep the experiment modest. Repeatedly exhausting a plan to prove its theoretical ceiling may consume more time than the decision is worth. A routine public-information recap and a high-consequence client deliverable can justify different choices. Record why a result was rejected, whether the problem was recoverable, and how long the correction took. Those observations make the next comparison better.

sections.heading: Tools, speed and reliability belong in the comparison
paragraphs: A model name does not describe the whole product. Verify whether the plan includes the browser, connectors, file creation, coding environment and automation surface your workflow needs. A subscription login and an API key can expose different features and billing paths. Do not assume access in one interface guarantees access in another.

Measure time to a usable result, interruptions and failed runs on your own tasks. Separate passive waiting from paid human attention so you do not count every background minute as labor. Do not turn a single session or a public benchmark into a reliability guarantee. Quality gates and missing required features should override a tempting price multiple.

sections.heading: Keep the spending boundary visible
paragraphs: Separate the base subscription from optional credits, API fallback, tools and taxes. Anthropic documents separately billed usage credits with spending controls. OpenAI distinguishes alerts from enforced API limits and warns that enforcement is not instantaneous. A budget notification is not proof that further charges are impossible.

PointCast should show the projected total and the reader’s chosen budget, but should never imply that its slider changes a provider’s settings. The calculator purchases nothing, enables no auto-reload and requests no credentials. If actual overage rates or plan coverage are unknown, it should say so instead of manufacturing a precise savings figure.

sections.heading: For client work, check the agreement
paragraphs: Consumer subscriptions, business workspaces and API services are different purchasing choices. Compare data-training settings, retention, access controls, approved integrations and the agreement governing the work. OpenAI’s API and business documentation and Anthropic’s commercial privacy documentation describe protections that should not be casually generalized to every consumer account.

For confidential client material, follow the client’s approved tools and data-handling rules. Avoid testing with sensitive files merely to benchmark a plan. Public or synthetic tasks can establish an initial baseline. A cheaper allowance is not a substitute for authorization, contractual fit or competent review.

sections.heading: The practical takeaway
paragraphs: Treat a large API-equivalent multiple as evidence about a particular allowance and workload, then test whether that workload resembles yours. Track a representative week, including the work that failed. Compare cash cost, accepted output and human time. Recheck the rate cards when models or plans change.

The best value is the capacity you can turn into reliable work. PointCast’s calculator should make assumptions visible, keep the arithmetic reproducible and leave room for an honest answer: there is not enough information yet to pick a winner.

claim_audit.source_description: User-supplied screenshot of an X post by @synthwavedd embedding a SemiAnalysis-branded chart
claim_audit.chart_status: Chart values transcribed from supplied screenshot; corresponding headline and methodology found in original public article; exact bar values not independently reproduced
claim_audit.workload_percentages_status: Do not infer from illegible tiny screenshot text. Do not substitute 96.6/2.6/0.8 without evidence.
claim_audit.top_tier_claim: The screenshot’s Astra/Fable comparison is a separate claim and is not established by its mid-tier chart. Do not publish its Fable model name as verified; official current pricing lists Fable 5.1.

calculator.title: AI value calculator
calculator.subtitle: Estimate the API cost of a workload and the cost of accepted work. No account connection needed.
calculator.execution: All arithmetic runs in the browser. No API calls, account access, uploads, paid model requests, telemetry of form values or automatic purchases.
calculator.privacy: Start in memory only. Optional Save on this device requires an explicit click; Clear removes saved values. Export only when requested by clicking Download assumptions. Do not put inputs in URL query strings or send them in analytics.
calculator.default_warning: Illustrative workload. Rates are dated reference presets; usage, quota coverage, quality and time inputs are assumptions, not provider promises.

modes.label: My workload
modes.purpose: Price a workload at chosen API rates; compare with an entered subscription cash total only when coverage is explicitly specified.

modes.label: Cost per accepted result
modes.purpose: Compare fully loaded costs for the same task definition and acceptance standard.

modes.label: Explore a published ceiling
modes.purpose: Optional advanced mode. Manually entered third-party ceilings with required source/date and utilization assumption. Disabled by default; never label as available credit or guaranteed savings.

inputs.help: Source-checked token rates only; does not imply plan eligibility or quota.
Include retries, failed attempts and abandoned runs; fractional averages allowed.
Ordinary uncached input only; exclude tokens counted as cache writes or cache reads.
Bill each token once in the provider’s applicable bucket. Enter writes across a full observed period; do not assume warm caches are free to create.
Include all billable output/reasoning categories according to the provider, not just visible text.
Tools, execution, storage and other non-token API charges. Zero means excluded, not verified free.

inputs.status: illustrative cash amount; matches some verified pre-tax plans but is editable

inputs.help: Credits, API fallback and required tools; avoid double counting.
There is no inferred token quota. If partly included, manually enter overage cost and confirm no omitted workload.
A finished task counted once after all attempts; must not exceed tasks started.
Only the share of waiting with a real opportunity cost; exclude time already counted as hands-on work.
Amortized integration/admin costs; keep comparison periods consistent.
Local planning threshold only. Does not configure provider spending controls.
Required if comparing full API cost; zero must be an explicit exclusion or observed zero.
Independent API-path time valuation, not inferred from subscription workflow.
Independent API-path accepted count for matched task scope.
Token plus per-attempt tools/compute charges; must reflect constant marginal price assumptions.
Required original source URL and observation date; third-party claim, never spendable credit.
Reader assumption. No default assumption that a ceiling is attainable.

equations.formula: token_cost_per_attempt = (input_tokens × input_rate + cache_read_tokens × cache_read_rate + cache_write_tokens × cache_write_rate + output_tokens × output_rate) / 1,000,000

equations.help: Same-workload list-price estimate; not provider compute cost, credits or realized savings.

equations.guard: Only display when quota_coverage is explicitly specified and cash cost > 0; label assumed or observed, never guaranteed.
Only with explicit coverage and matched scope; label modeled price difference, never money saved.
Accepted tasks must be > 0 and coverage known; otherwise display Not enough data or No accepted results, not infinity.
Optional comparison needs separately entered API-path quality/time/setup data; do not silently reuse subscription-path results.
Only if fixed, equal capability/scope and subscription capacity is known sufficient. If marginal cost = 0, display undefined. Disable if overage varies with workload.
A scenario sensitivity only; utilization in [0,1]; requires source/date and unchanged workload mix. Do not infer achievable scheduling or unused cash balance.

outputs: Token cost breakdown by category and total API-equivalent workload estimate
Subscription cash total, with included/excluded charges visible
Modeled price difference and multiple only if coverage is explicitly specified
Accepted tasks and fully loaded cost per accepted result
Time, quality and missing-required-feature notes alongside cost
Date-stamped source drawer; every numeric default labeled verified rate, user-entered, or hypothetical
Budget warning; explicit reminder this does not change provider settings
Low/base/high scenarios entered by the reader; no false statistical confidence interval
validation: Reject negative, non-finite or nonsensical values; do not silently convert blanks to zero.
Accepted tasks cannot exceed tasks started. Allow zero accepted tasks and explain why ratio is undefined.
All token buckets are mutually exclusive; reading and writing cached content in different requests is valid but a single billed event must not be counted twice.
Do not apply a universal cached share or convert message caps into monthly tokens.
Keep each provider’s measured token counts independent; same text can tokenize differently.
Use unrounded numbers internally; round only final display to cents or 2 decimal places.
Editable custom rates require a visible Custom/unverified label and optional source/date.
Do not generalize short-context or 5-minute-write rates to other modes; add separate rows/presets for distinct rate categories.
Hide winner badges if mandatory features, quality comparability or allowance coverage are unknown.
No account data, invoices, API keys or billing exports are required.

ux.layout: Three stacked panels on mobile: assumptions, result, sources. On desktop show two editable scenario columns and one shared task/acceptance brief.
ux.controls: Accessible labeled numeric fields, keyboard-friendly selects, units next to every input, aria-live polite results, reset examples button.
ux.claim_panel: Small expandable context card, not hero proof. Attribute the screenshot and link original analysis; display Reported API-equivalent ceiling, not cash benefit.
ux.privacy_notice: Your numbers stay in this browser. Saving on this device is optional.

worked_examples.title: A light, cache-heavy month
worked_examples.status: Hypothetical volumes and coverage; verified rate cards
worked_examples.interpretation: At these invented volumes, the token-only API estimates are below the $20 cash amount. This is not a purchase recommendation; tooling, time, taxes and capacity remain assumptions. No assertion that identical text consumes these same tokens. Cache writes are set to zero only to isolate the illustration; real estimates must include writes incurred over the measured period, and cache eligibility is not guaranteed.

worked_examples.title: Lose the cache hits
worked_examples.interpretation: The same nominal input volume costs about 4.49× E1 when all input is fresh. Changing cache behavior can dominate the comparison.

worked_examples.title: Human review changes the winner
worked_examples.interpretation: The higher cash-spend scenario has the lower full cost when it demonstrably saves three review hours. Do not invent those hours for a real comparison.

worked_examples.title: Ceiling is not realized value
worked_examples.status: Entirely hypothetical ceiling, not the source chart
worked_examples.interpretation: A headline 10× ceiling becomes 1× at 10% assumed utilization. This scales a fixed mix only and does not prove the schedule is achievable.

acceptance_tests: Default mode shows $9.80 token-only API estimate for GPT-6.1 Sol and suppresses savings/multiple because coverage is unknown.
E1 explicit assumed coverage produces 0.49×, not a 49% savings claim.
Zero accepted tasks never yields Infinity or NaN.
Blank rates produce Not enough data, not $0.
Changing one scenario does not change the other without an explicit Apply to both action.
All form input changes create no network requests.
Reload forgets form inputs unless Save on this device was explicitly selected.
Exported assumptions include source URLs, checked date, all inputs, all output labels and calculation version.

source_ledger.title: SemiAnalysis: Anthropic Subscriptions Offer 5x+ More Value Than OpenAI
source_ledger.status: Opened public article; paid dashboard and raw test logs not accessed
source_ledger.supports: Provider-meter experiments; September workload; partial-step exclusion; ±5% rate range; zero-meter-change assumption after 500M cache-read tokens.
source_ledger.caveat: Reported estimates are not independently replicated measurements. Exact workload percentages in the supplied image were not verified.

source_ledger.title: OpenAI API pricing
source_ledger.supports: GPT-6.1 Sol standard short-context input/cache-read/cache-write/output rates: $2/$0.10/$2.50/$10 per million tokens. Different processing and context tiers exist.

source_ledger.title: Claude API pricing
source_ledger.supports: Opus 5.5 standard input/cache-read/5-minute-write/1-hour-write/output rates: $4/$0.20/$5/$8/$20 per million tokens. Sonnet 5.5: $2/$0.20/$2.50/$4/$10. Tool and processing charges can differ.

source_ledger.title: ChatGPT Work and Codex pricing
source_ledger.status: Opened live page; stale search excerpts superseded
source_ledger.supports: Plus $20/month; Pro $100/$200/$500. Work and Codex share usage; current Pro has no five-hour limit; weekly limits may apply. API rates do not establish included tasks. Credit billing differs from API billing.

source_ledger.title: Claude pricing
source_ledger.supports: Pro $20 monthly or $200 billed annually; Max begins at $100. Feature access, consumer/commercial distinctions, Fable restrictions, and prices exclude applicable taxes.

source_ledger.title: What is the Max plan?
source_ledger.supports: Web Max 5x $100/month, Max 20x $200/month; five-hour and weekly limits; further limits possible; mobile price can differ.

source_ledger.title: How do usage and length limits work?
source_ledger.supports: Model, effort, conversation complexity and tools affect usage; Claude surfaces share allowance. Context-window length is distinct from usage capacity.

source_ledger.title: OpenAI prompt caching
source_ledger.supports: GPT-5.6-and-later cache writes and reads have separate treatment; GPT-6.1 Sol read multiplier is 0.05 of base input. Cache matching and breakpoints matter.

source_ledger.title: Manage usage credits for paid Claude plans
source_ledger.supports: Optional extra usage is separate from the subscription; standard API pricing applies; monthly spending caps, alerts and auto-reload are distinct controls.

source_ledger.title: OpenAI API spend limits
source_ledger.supports: Alerts do not stop usage; hard limits can stop affected requests; enforcement latency permits a small overrun.

source_ledger.title: Data controls in the OpenAI platform
source_ledger.supports: API data is not used for model training by default; retention and application state require separate review.

source_ledger.title: ChatGPT Work cloud security
source_ledger.supports: Business, Enterprise and Edu protections, permissions, retention and audit controls differ by configuration; business data not used for training by default.

source_ledger.title: Anthropic commercial data and model training
source_ledger.supports: Commercial products distinguished from consumer plans; chats and coding sessions excluded from training unless opted in, including explicit feedback and programs.

source_ledger.title: Claude Agent SDK with your Claude plan
source_ledger.supports: June 15 change paused; current top notice says SDK, claude -p and third-party usage still draw from subscription limits; announced monthly credit unavailable.
source_ledger.caveat: Historical body below the pause notice must not be treated as current policy.
